事務 covers clerical and administrative work such as records, forms, scheduling, and correspondence, not the physical office itself.
words.readingMnemonic: An accountant wheels a filing cabinet into a <reading>GYM</reading> and starts doing paperwork between squats. The weights vanish under forms as the gym becomes an <vocabulary>office work</vocabulary> department. 事務 refers to clerical or administrative work.

contextSentences.ja: 午前中は事務の仕事をします。
contextSentences.en: I do office work in the morning.

contextSentences.ja: 事務を担当する人に聞いてください。
contextSentences.en: Please ask the person in charge of administration.

words.meaningMnemonic:
<kanji>Return home</kanji> to <kanji>conserve</kanji> your family ties; the trip is a <vocabulary>return to one's hometown</vocabulary>, or <vocabulary>homecoming</vocabulary>.

帰省 means temporarily going back to one's home region to visit family, especially during holidays such as New Year or Obon.
words.readingMnemonic: Your childhood house key begins to <reading>KEY—SAY</reading>, “Come home!” every holiday. Its command is clear: <vocabulary>return to one's hometown</vocabulary>. 帰省 is specifically a homecoming to one's family home or hometown.

contextSentences.ja: 年末に家族で故郷へ帰省します。
contextSentences.en: My family and I will return to our hometown at the end of the year.

contextSentences.ja: 夏休みの帰省で友達に会った。
contextSentences.en: I met friends while home for summer vacation.

words.meaningMnemonic:
When workers <kanji>cut off</kanji> the <kanji>water</kanji>, the empty pipes announce a <vocabulary>water outage</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>water shutoff</vocabulary>.

断水 can be planned for maintenance or caused by damage; 断水する describes the supply being interrupted.
words.readingMnemonic: Sever 断 carries だん as it swings an axe through water 水 carrying すい: <reading>だん—すい</reading>. The cut main leaves every pipe empty in a complete <vocabulary>water outage</vocabulary>. 断水 can be a planned shutoff or an unexpected loss of water service.

contextSentences.ja: 工事のため午後は断水します。
contextSentences.en: The water will be shut off this afternoon for construction.

contextSentences.ja: 断水に備えて水をためた。
contextSentences.en: I stored water in preparation for the outage.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Take every <kanji>point</kanji> in turn and <kanji>examine</kanji> it; you perform an <vocabulary>inspection</vocabulary> or thorough <vocabulary>check</vocabulary>.

点検 is a systematic safety or maintenance check of equipment, vehicles, buildings, or systems.
words.readingMnemonic: Ken lines up ten machines and checks each with a magnifying glass: <reading>TEN—KEN</reading>. One loose bolt fails the <vocabulary>inspection</vocabulary> and sets off every alarm. 点検 is a systematic check of equipment, facilities, or condition.

contextSentences.ja: 旅行の前に車を点検した。
contextSentences.en: I inspected the car before the trip.

contextSentences.ja: 設備の定期点検を行います。
contextSentences.en: We will perform a regular inspection of the equipment.

words.meaningMnemonic:
<kanji>Investigate</kanji> a matter, then <kanji>inspect</kanji> the evidence; together those actions form an <vocabulary>investigation</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>survey</vocabulary>.

調査 covers deliberate fact-finding through research, questioning, measurement, or surveys, and is commonly used with 調査する.
words.readingMnemonic: INVESTIGATE 調 unlocks a case file while INSPECT 査 searches every drawer; their familiar sounds join as <reading>ちょう—さ</reading>. Hidden evidence spills across the desk and launches a full <vocabulary>investigation</vocabulary>. 調査する covers investigating facts or conducting research.

contextSentences.ja: 市は住民の意見を調査した。
contextSentences.en: The city surveyed its residents' opinions.

contextSentences.ja: 事故の原因を詳しく調査している。
contextSentences.en: They are investigating the cause of the accident in detail.

words.meaningMnemonic:
The place where you <kanji>lie down</kanji> is its own <kanji>room</kanji>: the <vocabulary>bedroom</vocabulary>.

寝室 specifically names a sleeping room and sounds more descriptive or formal than casually saying the room where someone sleeps.
words.readingMnemonic: Sleep 寝 carries しん into a room 室 carrying しつ: <reading>しん—しつ</reading>. A mountain of sheets bursts through the door, and the giant bed beneath leaves no doubt this is the <vocabulary>bedroom</vocabulary>. 寝室 is specifically a room used for sleeping.

contextSentences.ja: 寝室の窓を少し開けた。
contextSentences.en: I opened the bedroom window a little.

contextSentences.ja: 寝室にはベッドが二つある。
contextSentences.en: There are two beds in the bedroom.

words.meaningMnemonic:
At the service counter, <kanji>respond</kanji> to the person <kanji>opposite</kanji> you and <vocabulary>attend to</vocabulary> them, especially when you <vocabulary>deal with customers</vocabulary>.

応対 describes how someone receives and handles another person, particularly a visitor, caller, or customer; it often carries an evaluation such as polite or poor.
words.readingMnemonic: A customer arrives tangled in a necktie, and the clerk cries <reading>OH—TIE!</reading> She patiently untangles him to show how to <vocabulary>deal with customers</vocabulary>. 応対 focuses on attending and responding to people, often in service work.

contextSentences.ja: あの店員の応対は丁寧だった。
contextSentences.en: That clerk's customer service was polite.

contextSentences.ja: 今日は私が電話の応対をします。
contextSentences.en: I will handle the phone calls today.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Take your <kanji>main</kanji> point and <kanji>stretch</kanji> it out where everyone can see it: you <vocabulary>assert</vocabulary> a <vocabulary>claim</vocabulary>.

主張 can be the position itself or the act of stating it firmly; it does not necessarily imply that the claim is correct.
words.readingMnemonic: MASTER 主 grabs STRETCH 張 and pulls a banner across the debate hall; their familiar sounds join as <reading>しゅ—ちょう</reading>. The banner displays one enormous <vocabulary>claim</vocabulary> that the speaker loudly asserts. 主張 is a stated position or assertion, not merely casual conversation.

contextSentences.ja: 会議で自分の意見を主張した。
contextSentences.en: I asserted my opinion at the meeting.

contextSentences.ja: 会社は製品の安全性を主張している。
contextSentences.en: The company claims that its product is safe.

words.meaningMnemonic:
<kanji>Call</kanji> air toward you, then <kanji>suck</kanji> it in and release it; that cycle is <vocabulary>breathing</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>respiration</vocabulary>.

呼吸 is the biological process or a breath rhythm, and 呼吸する means to breathe.
words.readingMnemonic: Call 呼 carries こ into a rooster's beak, while inhale 吸 carries きゅう into its chest: <reading>こ—きゅう</reading>. The rooster inhales, crows, and makes its whole body demonstrate <vocabulary>breathing</vocabulary>. 呼吸 covers both a breath and the ongoing act of respiration.

contextSentences.ja: ゆっくり深い呼吸をしてください。
contextSentences.en: Please breathe slowly and deeply.

contextSentences.ja: 走った後は呼吸が速くなる。
contextSentences.en: Your breathing becomes faster after running.

words.meaningMnemonic:
<kanji>Return home</kanji> to your <kanji>house</kanji> and you <vocabulary>go home</vocabulary>; the arrival is your <vocabulary>return home</vocabulary>.

帰宅 focuses on returning to one's residence and is common in schedules and reports, as in 七時ごろ帰宅する.
words.readingMnemonic: A commuter finds her house <reading>KEY—TACK</reading> pinned to the station board. She grabs it and races to <vocabulary>return home</vocabulary> before the door locks. 帰宅する means to go or come back to one's home.

contextSentences.ja: 今日は七時ごろ帰宅します。
contextSentences.en: I will get home around seven today.

contextSentences.ja: 帰宅したら連絡してください。
contextSentences.en: Please contact me when you get home.

words.meaningMnemonic:
<kanji>Determine</kanji> a straight <kanji>standard</kanji> for every line with a <vocabulary>ruler</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>straightedge</vocabulary>.

定規 is the physical measuring or drawing tool; use it with 線を引く for drawing a line.
words.readingMnemonic: Joe drags a perfectly straight ruler through a tub of ghee: <reading>JOE—GHEE</reading>. Every golden stripe remains straight because the <vocabulary>ruler</vocabulary> refuses to bend. 定規 is a measuring ruler or straightedge; 規 is voiced to ぎ in this established word.

contextSentences.ja: 定規で線を引いてください。
contextSentences.en: Please draw a line with a ruler.

contextSentences.ja: 三十センチの定規を買った。
contextSentences.en: I bought a thirty-centimeter ruler.

words.meaningMnemonic:
<kanji>Expand</kanji> the collection across a hall and <kanji>indicate</kanji> what visitors should notice: it becomes an <vocabulary>exhibition</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>display</vocabulary>.

展示 is the public presentation of objects or information; 展示する is to put something on display.
words.readingMnemonic: Exhibit 展 carries てん as it opens ten glass cases, and show 示 carries じ as it points a spotlight at each one: <reading>てん—じ</reading>. The objects become the museum's strangest <vocabulary>exhibition</vocabulary> and public display. 展示する means to exhibit objects or information.

contextSentences.ja: 博物館で古い道具を展示している。
contextSentences.en: The museum is displaying old tools.

contextSentences.ja: 写真の展示は日曜日までです。
contextSentences.en: The photography exhibition runs through Sunday.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Compare what the engine <kanji>burn</kanji>s with the resulting <kanji>expense</kanji> and you get its <vocabulary>fuel economy</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>gas mileage</vocabulary>.

燃費 describes distance or performance per amount of fuel; 燃費がいい means fuel-efficient, not expensive.
words.readingMnemonic: Fuel-burning 燃 carries ねん into a tiny PEA that powers a car: <reading>ねん—PEA</reading>. One pea carries the car a hundred kilometers, giving it miraculous <vocabulary>fuel economy</vocabulary>. 燃費がいい means fuel-efficient; 燃費が悪い means poor fuel economy.

contextSentences.ja: この車は燃費がいい。
contextSentences.en: This car gets good gas mileage.

contextSentences.ja: 燃費を比べて車を選んだ。
contextSentences.en: I chose a car after comparing fuel economy.

words.meaningMnemonic:
For each unit of <kanji>time</kanji>, your employer supplies a <kanji>salary</kanji>: an <vocabulary>hourly wage</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>hourly pay</vocabulary>.

時給 states pay per hour and commonly appears with an amount, such as 時給千二百円.
words.readingMnemonic: A giant letter G waits for the factory clock's cue: <reading>G—CUE</reading>. Each hourly cue drops another coin into the worker's <vocabulary>hourly pay</vocabulary> bucket. 時給 is the wage amount earned per hour.

contextSentences.ja: この仕事の時給は千二百円です。
contextSentences.en: This job pays 1,200 yen per hour.

contextSentences.ja: 来月から時給が上がる。
contextSentences.en: My hourly wage will go up next month.

words.meaningMnemonic:
To <kanji>prosper</kanji>, the body must <kanji>foster</kanji> itself with <vocabulary>nutrition</vocabulary> and <vocabulary>nourishment</vocabulary>.

栄養 refers to nutrients collectively or the nourishment food provides; 栄養がある describes something nutritious.
words.readingMnemonic: A nutritionist fires vitamins at a giant letter A and yells <reading>A—YO!</reading> Every colorful capsule lands in a meal and supplies its <vocabulary>nutrition</vocabulary>. 栄養 refers to nourishment or nutrients that support health and growth.

contextSentences.ja: 野菜には栄養がたくさんある。
contextSentences.en: Vegetables contain plenty of nutrition.

contextSentences.ja: 栄養のバランスを考えて食べる。
contextSentences.en: I eat with nutritional balance in mind.

words.meaningMnemonic:
The school pays a daily <kanji>salary</kanji> in things to <kanji>eat</kanji>: its <vocabulary>school lunch</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>meal service</vocabulary>.

給食 is an institutionally provided meal, especially at school, but it can also refer to meal service at a workplace, hospital, or other facility.
words.readingMnemonic: The school bell gives a cue, then the lunch cart crashes through the wall: <reading>CUE—SHOCK!</reading> The spectacular entrance delivers today's <vocabulary>school lunch</vocabulary>. 給食 is an organized meal service, especially at schools and institutions.

contextSentences.ja: 今日の給食はカレーです。
contextSentences.en: Today's school lunch is curry.

contextSentences.ja: この学校では無料の給食を出している。
contextSentences.en: This school provides free meals.

packs.title: Everyday Kanji: Levels 26–30
packs.description: High-utility everyday vocabulary whose newest WaniKani kanji falls between levels 26 and 30.

words.meaningMnemonic:
A <kanji>seal</kanji> shaped like an <kanji>elephant</kanji> stamps an unforgettable image into your mind, leaving an <vocabulary>impression</vocabulary>.

印象 is the mental effect a person, place, or experience gives you, as in 明るい印象 or 印象に残る.
words.readingMnemonic: An actor steps <reading>IN—SHOW</reading> wearing a hat made of fireworks. That first image burns a lasting <vocabulary>impression</vocabulary> into the audience's memory. 印象 is the impression a person, thing, or experience leaves.

contextSentences.ja: 彼は明るい印象を与えた。
contextSentences.en: He gave a cheerful impression.

contextSentences.ja: 最初の印象と今の印象は全く違う。
contextSentences.en: My impression now is completely different from my first impression.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Your <kanji>hand</kanji> follows the <kanji>steps</kanji> toward a goal; that chosen route is a <vocabulary>means</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>method</vocabulary>.

手段 emphasizes the practical way or instrument used to achieve an end, as in 交通手段 or 目的のための手段.
words.readingMnemonic: Dan crosses a river using only a giant shoe: <reading>SHOE—DAN</reading>. The shoe is his ridiculous <vocabulary>means</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>method</vocabulary> of reaching the other bank. 手段 is a practical means for achieving an end.

contextSentences.ja: 電車は最も便利な移動手段です。
contextSentences.en: The train is the most convenient means of transportation.

contextSentences.ja: 目的を達成するための手段を考えた。
contextSentences.en: I thought of a method for achieving the goal.

words.meaningMnemonic:
<kanji>Cool</kanji> something until it is completely <kanji>frozen</kanji>; that process is <vocabulary>freezing</vocabulary>, and the result is <vocabulary>frozen</vocabulary>.

冷凍 refers to freezing for preservation and appears in 冷凍する, 冷凍食品, and 冷凍庫.
words.readingMnemonic: A freezing ray hits your toe while a villain cackles <reading>RAY—TOE!</reading> Your boot turns solid, perfectly <vocabulary>frozen</vocabulary> to the ground. 冷凍 is freezing for preservation or something kept frozen.

contextSentences.ja: 残ったご飯を冷凍した。
contextSentences.en: I froze the leftover rice.

contextSentences.ja: 冷凍の野菜は長く保存できる。
contextSentences.en: Frozen vegetables can be stored for a long time.

words.meaningMnemonic:
<kanji>Draw near</kanji> an interesting shop by stepping off your usual <kanji>road</kanji>; that <vocabulary>detour</vocabulary> is a <vocabulary>stop on the way</vocabulary>.

寄り道 is a small diversion while traveling somewhere, often an unplanned stop before going home or reaching the main destination.
words.readingMnemonic: Draw near 寄り carries より off the main road, while road 道 carries みち down a side street: <reading>より—みち</reading>. A traveler follows them and turns one stop into a delicious <vocabulary>detour</vocabulary>. 寄り道 is a side trip or stop made on the way somewhere.

contextSentences.ja: 帰りに本屋へ寄り道した。
contextSentences.en: I stopped at a bookstore on the way home.

contextSentences.ja: 寄り道しないで早く帰ってきて。
contextSentences.en: Come straight home without making any detours.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Make a <kanji>suitable</kanji> <kanji>cut</kanji> so the choice fits the situation exactly; it is <vocabulary>appropriate</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>suitable</vocabulary>.

適切 is a fairly neutral-to-formal evaluation that a method, response, amount, or expression properly fits the circumstances.
words.readingMnemonic: A techie adjusts a control room while the supervisor chants <reading>TECHIE SETS</reading>. Each dial clicks into the most <vocabulary>appropriate</vocabulary> and <vocabulary>suitable</vocabulary> position. 適切 describes something fitting the situation or purpose.

contextSentences.ja: 状況に応じて適切な方法を選んでください。
contextSentences.en: Please choose an appropriate method for the situation.

contextSentences.ja: 先生は質問に適切に答えた。
contextSentences.en: The teacher answered the question appropriately.

packs.title: Everyday Kanji: Levels 31–35
packs.description: High-utility everyday vocabulary whose newest WaniKani kanji falls between levels 31 and 35.

words.meaningMnemonic:
A piece of <kanji>writing</kanji> has a <kanji>vein</kanji> running through it; follow that vein to understand its <vocabulary>context</vocabulary> and <vocabulary>line of thought</vocabulary>.

文脈 is the surrounding linguistic or situational context that makes an expression intelligible, as in 文脈から意味を判断する.
words.readingMnemonic: A bun rolls into a sentence, a cat meows, and a cuckoo answers: <reading>BUN—MEOW—COO</reading>. Only the surrounding words explain why this nonsense belongs there, revealing the <vocabulary>context</vocabulary>. 文脈 is the linguistic or logical thread around an expression.

contextSentences.ja: 文脈から言葉の意味を考えた。
contextSentences.en: I inferred the word's meaning from the context.

contextSentences.ja: その一文だけでは文脈が分からない。
contextSentences.en: You cannot understand the context from that one sentence alone.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Make the space <kanji>pure</kanji>: <kanji>sweep</kanji> every surface until the <vocabulary>cleaning</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>cleanup</vocabulary> is complete.

清掃 is systematic cleaning of a place or facility and sounds more formal or work-oriented than everyday 掃除.
words.readingMnemonic: A cleaner orders a mountain of dirty curtains, <reading>SAY—SEW!</reading> Each repaired curtain sweeps the floor behind it, completing the <vocabulary>cleanup</vocabulary>. 清掃 is organized cleaning of a place or facility.

contextSentences.ja: 毎朝、駅の清掃をしています。
contextSentences.en: We clean the station every morning.

contextSentences.ja: 海岸の清掃に参加した。
contextSentences.en: I took part in a beach cleanup.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Take the action to <kanji>knit</kanji> and produce a warm <kanji>thing</kanji>: <vocabulary>knitting</vocabulary> or a <vocabulary>knitted item</vocabulary>.

編み物 can name the craft itself or an object made by knitting, with context distinguishing the activity from the finished piece.
words.readingMnemonic: Knit 編み carries あみ into a box, and thing 物 carries もの out wearing a half-finished scarf: <reading>あみ—もの</reading>. The scarf keeps growing until the <vocabulary>knitting</vocabulary> buries the room. 編み物 can mean the activity or the thing being knitted.

contextSentences.ja: 祖母は編み物が得意です。
contextSentences.en: My grandmother is good at knitting.

contextSentences.ja: 冬の間に編み物を始めた。
contextSentences.en: I took up knitting during the winter.

words.meaningMnemonic:
<kanji>Mix</kanji> people together in a <kanji>random</kanji> tangle; the result is <vocabulary>crowding</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>congestion</vocabulary>.

混雑 describes a place or transport system being crowded; 混雑する means to become or be congested.
words.readingMnemonic: Mix 混 carries こん into a station, while clutter 雑 carries ざつ through every gate: <reading>こん—ざつ</reading>. Commuters and luggage tangle together in instant <vocabulary>crowding</vocabulary> and congestion. 混雑 describes a place or traffic being crowded.

contextSentences.ja: 朝の電車はとても混雑する。
contextSentences.en: Morning trains get very crowded.

contextSentences.ja: 混雑を避けて早く出発した。
contextSentences.en: We left early to avoid congestion.

words.meaningMnemonic:
<kanji>Say humbly</kanji> what you want and send it <kanji>into</kanji> the office; the result is an <vocabulary>application</vocabulary>, <vocabulary>registration</vocabulary>, or <vocabulary>request</vocabulary>.

申し込み is the submitted request or act of signing up; 申し込む is the corresponding verb, and Xの申し込み is an application for X.
words.readingMnemonic: State humbly 申し carries もうし onto a form, and enter 込み carries こみ through the registration slot: <reading>もうし—こみ</reading>. A giant stamp lands on the <vocabulary>application</vocabulary> and registers its owner. 申し込み is an application, registration, or formal request to participate or receive something.

contextSentences.ja: 講座の申し込みは明日までです。
contextSentences.en: Applications for the course close tomorrow.

contextSentences.ja: オンラインで申し込みを済ませた。
contextSentences.en: I completed the registration online.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Make the rice <kanji>big</kanji> by adding another <kanji>pile</kanji> on top and you get a <vocabulary>large serving</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>large portion</vocabulary>.

大盛り is a larger-than-standard serving, especially of rice, noodles, or a restaurant dish; 大盛りにする asks to upsize it.
words.readingMnemonic: Big 大 carries おお into a rice bowl, and heap 盛り carries もり onto the top: <reading>おお—もり</reading>. The rice rises into a mountain-sized <vocabulary>large serving</vocabulary>. 大盛り is a larger-than-standard serving, especially at a restaurant.

contextSentences.ja: ご飯を大盛りでお願いします。
contextSentences.en: A large serving of rice, please.

contextSentences.ja: 大盛りのカレーを全部食べた。
contextSentences.en: I ate the entire large portion of curry.

words.meaningMnemonic:
A field of <kanji>sand</kanji> running along the <kanji>beach</kanji> is a <vocabulary>sandy beach</vocabulary>.

砂浜 specifically means a stretch of sandy shore, in contrast with a rocky or concrete waterfront.
words.readingMnemonic: Sue finds someone hammering the shore and protests, <reading>SUE—NAH—HAMMER!</reading> She buries the hammer in the <vocabulary>sandy beach</vocabulary> before it can crack another shell. 砂浜 is a beach or shore covered in sand.

contextSentences.ja: 子どもたちが砂浜で遊んでいる。
contextSentences.en: The children are playing on the sandy beach.

contextSentences.ja: 朝早く砂浜を散歩した。
contextSentences.en: I walked along the beach early in the morning.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Add す to <kanji>steam</kanji> and turn the rising vapor into an action: to <vocabulary>steam</vocabulary> food.

蒸す is a transitive verb for cooking or heating something with steam, as in 野菜を蒸す.
words.readingMnemonic: A giant <reading>MOOSE</reading> sits on a pot lid until clouds billow from every edge. Its weight traps the heat to <vocabulary>steam</vocabulary> the dumplings inside. 蒸す is the transitive verb for steaming food; it can also describe muggy weather in intransitive use.

contextSentences.ja: 野菜を蒸すと甘くなる。
contextSentences.en: Steaming vegetables makes them sweeter.

contextSentences.ja: 魚を蒸すと、身が柔らかくなる。
contextSentences.en: Steaming fish makes the flesh tender.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Make your <kanji>exit</kanji> from home to perform your <kanji>work</kanji> duty and you <vocabulary>go to work</vocabulary>; your presence is <vocabulary>attendance at work</vocabulary>.

出勤 focuses on reporting for work and contrasts with 退勤, leaving work, and 欠勤, absence.
words.readingMnemonic: A work alarm <reading>SHOOK—KIN</reading> out of bed and straight through the office door. Every relative tumbles in to <vocabulary>go to work</vocabulary>. 出勤する means to go in or be present at work, not the generic act of working.

contextSentences.ja: 毎朝八時に出勤する。
contextSentences.en: I go to work at eight every morning.

contextSentences.ja: 今日は自転車で出勤した。
contextSentences.en: I went to work by bicycle today.

words.meaningMnemonic:
A precise <kanji>time</kanji> <kanji>carve</kanji>d into the timetable gives the exact <vocabulary>time</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>hour</vocabulary>.

時刻 refers to a specific clock time, especially in schedules and announcements, rather than time as an abstract concept.
words.readingMnemonic: Time 時 carries じ onto a clock, while carve 刻 carries こく into its face: <reading>じ—こく</reading>. The carving glows to announce one exact <vocabulary>time</vocabulary>. 時刻 is a specific clock time, often scheduled or recorded.

contextSentences.ja: 電車の出発時刻を調べた。
contextSentences.en: I checked the train's departure time.

contextSentences.ja: 約束の時刻に間に合った。
contextSentences.en: I made it in time for our appointment.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Give the class a <kanji>rest</kanji> instead of a <kanji>lecture</kanji> and the result is a <vocabulary>class cancellation</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>cancelled lecture</vocabulary>.

休講 means a scheduled class or lecture will not be held, typically because of the instructor or institution; 休講になる means it gets cancelled.
words.readingMnemonic: The professor sees a glowing cue from headquarters, Co.: <reading>CUE—CO.</reading> He pulls a curtain across the classroom and declares a <vocabulary>class cancellation</vocabulary>. 休講 means that a scheduled class or lecture will not be held.

contextSentences.ja: 先生が病気で今日は休講です。
contextSentences.en: Today's class is cancelled because the teacher is ill.

contextSentences.ja: 休講のお知らせを学生に送った。
contextSentences.en: We sent the students a class-cancellation notice.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Let your movement <kanji>stagnate</kanji> while you <kanji>exist</kanji> in one place; that period is a <vocabulary>stay</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>sojourn</vocabulary>.

滞在 is a temporary stay away from one's usual home, often stated with a place and duration and used as 滞在する.
words.readingMnemonic: Stay 滞 carries たい into a hotel, while exist 在 carries ざい into a suitcase: <reading>たい—ざい</reading>. The luggage unpacks furniture because this will be a long <vocabulary>stay</vocabulary>. 滞在 is staying temporarily in a place away from home.

contextSentences.ja: 京都に三日間滞在した。
contextSentences.en: I stayed in Kyoto for three days.

contextSentences.ja: 滞在中はこのホテルを利用します。
contextSentences.en: I will use this hotel during my stay.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Let the vehicle <kanji>carry</kanji> you, then pay it <kanji>rent</kanji> for the ride: the <vocabulary>fare</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>passenger fare</vocabulary>.

運賃 is the charge for passenger transportation by train, bus, taxi, and similar services; it does not mean a general fee.
words.readingMnemonic: Carry 運 brings うん onto a bus, while fare 賃 brings ちん into the fare box: <reading>うん—ちん</reading>. The doors open only when the full <vocabulary>fare</vocabulary> drops inside. 運賃 is the passenger fare for transportation.

contextSentences.ja: バスの運賃を現金で払った。
contextSentences.en: I paid the bus fare in cash.

contextSentences.ja: 子どもの運賃は大人の半額です。
contextSentences.en: The child fare is half the adult fare.

packs.title: Everyday Kanji: Levels 36–40
packs.description: High-utility everyday vocabulary whose newest WaniKani kanji falls between levels 36 and 40.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Stop your <kanji>ride</kanji> and <kanji>exchange</kanji> one vehicle for another; you <vocabulary>change trains</vocabulary>, and the connection is a <vocabulary>transfer</vocabulary>.

乗り換え is the transfer itself or transfer point between trains, buses, or other transport; 乗り換える is the verb.
words.readingMnemonic: Ride 乗り carries のり onto a train, while switch 換え carries かえ to the next platform: <reading>のり—かえ</reading>. The first train vanishes, forcing a <vocabulary>transfer</vocabulary> to another line. 乗り換え can also be a transfer between buses or other transport.

contextSentences.ja: 新宿で地下鉄に乗り換えます。
contextSentences.en: I will transfer to the subway at Shinjuku.

contextSentences.ja: この乗り換えには五分かかる。
contextSentences.en: This transfer takes five minutes.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Two sides <kanji>mix</kanji> at the table and <kanji>exchange</kanji> what they brought; that is an <vocabulary>exchange</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>swap</vocabulary>.

交換 is a mutual replacement or trade of objects, information, parts, or opinions and commonly forms 交換する.
words.readingMnemonic: A company called Co. trades its empty can for a full one: <reading>CO.—CAN</reading>. The cans swap places and complete the <vocabulary>exchange</vocabulary>. 交換する means to exchange things, information, or parts for one another.

contextSentences.ja: 友達と連絡先を交換した。
contextSentences.en: I exchanged contact information with a friend.

contextSentences.ja: 壊れた商品を新しいものに交換してもらった。
contextSentences.en: I had the defective product exchanged for a new one.

words.meaningMnemonic:
<kanji>Step</kanji> across the <kanji>cut</kanji> where tracks slice through the road and you are at a <vocabulary>railway crossing</vocabulary>.

踏切 is a level crossing where a road or path meets railway tracks, usually with gates, lights, or warning bells.
words.readingMnemonic: Tread 踏み carries ふみ toward the tracks, while cut 切り carries きり across the road: <reading>ふみ—きり</reading>. A striped gate slices traffic in two at the <vocabulary>railway crossing</vocabulary>. 踏切 is the crossing itself, not the act of stepping and cutting.

contextSentences.ja: 踏切で電車が通るのを待った。
contextSentences.en: I waited at the railway crossing for the train to pass.

contextSentences.ja: この踏切は朝とても混む。
contextSentences.en: This railway crossing gets very crowded in the morning.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Write the <kanji>address</kanji> that sends the message <kanji>ahead</kanji> to its <vocabulary>destination</vocabulary>.

宛先 is the recipient address or destination field on an envelope, parcel, email, or electronic message.
words.readingMnemonic: Destination 宛 carries あて onto an envelope, while ahead 先 carries さき toward the recipient: <reading>あて—さき</reading>. Without those details, the <vocabulary>address</vocabulary> spins in circles and never arrives. 宛先 is the recipient or destination information written on mail or a message.

contextSentences.ja: 封筒に宛先を書いてください。
contextSentences.en: Please write the address on the envelope.

contextSentences.ja: メールの宛先を間違えた。
contextSentences.en: I entered the wrong email address.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Gather every loose <kanji>fragment</kanji> and <kanji>attach</kanji> it to its proper place; you <vocabulary>tidy up</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>put away</vocabulary> the mess.

片付ける is a transitive verb for putting objects away, clearing a space, or finishing off a task or problem.
words.readingMnemonic: One loose piece 片 carries かた across a messy room, then attach 付ける carries つける toward its proper place. The pieces collide and voice つ to づ in <reading>かた—づける</reading>, clicking every object home as they <vocabulary>tidy up</vocabulary> the room. 片付ける can mean putting things away or finishing a matter.

contextSentences.ja: 食事の後で台所を片付ける。
contextSentences.en: I tidy the kitchen after the meal.

contextSentences.ja: 机の上の本を片付ける。
contextSentences.en: I put away the books on the desk.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Make a temporary <kanji>resident</kanji> of your <kanji>car</kanji> and you <vocabulary>park a vehicle</vocabulary>; the act is <vocabulary>parking</vocabulary>.

駐車 refers specifically to parking a vehicle; 駐車する is to park, and 駐車場 is a parking lot.
words.readingMnemonic: At a car park, an attendant gives every vehicle a giant 注射, an injection. That exact homophone <reading>ちゅうしゃ</reading> pins each car in place, forcing every driver to <vocabulary>park a vehicle</vocabulary>. 駐車 means parking a vehicle; 注射 is the medical injection with the same reading.

contextSentences.ja: ここに車を駐車しないでください。
contextSentences.en: Please do not park a car here.

contextSentences.ja: 駅の近くに駐車する場所がない。
contextSentences.en: There is nowhere to park near the station.

packs.title: Everyday Kanji: Levels 41–45
packs.description: High-utility everyday vocabulary whose newest WaniKani kanji falls between levels 41 and 45.

words.meaningMnemonic:
<kanji>Wrap</kanji> a soft <kanji>belt</kanji> around an injury and it becomes a <vocabulary>bandage</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>dressing</vocabulary>.

包帯 is the strip or dressing wrapped around a wound or injured area; 包帯を巻く means to apply one.
words.readingMnemonic: A gardener wraps a bleeding hoe in a necktie: <reading>HOE—TIE</reading>. The ridiculous cloth becomes a makeshift <vocabulary>bandage</vocabulary> around the blade. 包帯 is a medical bandage or dressing.

contextSentences.ja: 傷に包帯を巻いた。
contextSentences.en: I wrapped a bandage around the wound.

contextSentences.ja: 濡れた包帯を新しいものに替えた。
contextSentences.en: I replaced the wet dressing with a new one.

words.meaningMnemonic:
<kanji>Attain</kanji> the point where everyone must <kanji>hurry</kanji>: the matter is <vocabulary>urgent</vocabulary> and must be handled <vocabulary>immediately</vocabulary>.

至急 is forceful and businesslike, common in messages and instructions that require prompt action, such as 至急ご連絡ください.
words.readingMnemonic: A stage manager points at an actor and yells <reading>SHE—CUE!</reading> The emergency curtain is falling, so she must move <vocabulary>immediately</vocabulary>. 至急 marks something as urgent or needing prompt action.

contextSentences.ja: 至急、折り返し電話してください。
contextSentences.en: Please call me back immediately.

contextSentences.ja: 至急の用件があるそうです。
contextSentences.en: Apparently there is an urgent matter.

words.meaningMnemonic:
The way you <kanji>go</kanji> through a formal <kanji>ceremony</kanji> reveals your <vocabulary>manners</vocabulary> and <vocabulary>behavior</vocabulary>.

行儀 evaluates socially proper conduct, especially at meals or for children and animals; 行儀がいい means well-behaved.
words.readingMnemonic: Go 行 carries ぎょう to the dinner table, while ceremony 儀 carries ぎ into a perfect bow: <reading>ぎょう—ぎ</reading>. Even a gyoza bows before every bite, and its flawless table <vocabulary>manners</vocabulary> shame the rude diners. 行儀 usually refers to socially proper behavior, especially posture or manners.

contextSentences.ja: 食事中の行儀に気をつけなさい。
contextSentences.en: Mind your manners while eating.

contextSentences.ja: 犬が行儀よく座って待っている。
contextSentences.en: The dog is sitting and waiting obediently.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Your <kanji>liver</kanji> and <kanji>heart</kanji> are both vital, so whatever is compared to them must be <vocabulary>essential</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>crucial</vocabulary>.

肝心 singles out the most important point or thing in a situation, often in 肝心なのは, the essential thing is.
words.readingMnemonic: A scientist opens a tin marked <reading>CAN—GENE</reading> and finds the only gene that can save the crop. Losing that can would destroy the experiment, so it is absolutely <vocabulary>crucial</vocabulary>. 肝心 describes the essential or most important point.

contextSentences.ja: 肝心な鍵を家に忘れた。
contextSentences.en: I left the crucial key at home.

contextSentences.ja: 肝心なのは毎日続けることです。
contextSentences.en: The essential thing is to continue every day.

words.meaningMnemonic:
If your hand or your words can <kanji>slide</kanji> without catching, they are <vocabulary>smooth</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>fluent</vocabulary>.

滑らか describes an even physical texture or movement and, figuratively, speech or transitions that flow naturally.
words.readingMnemonic: Four polishers attack a jagged stone: one objects ‘NAH!’, a sheep bleats ‘MEH!’, a cheerleader shouts ‘RAH!’, and a crow adds ‘CAW!’ Their chant <reading>NAH—MEH—RAH—CAW</reading> continues until the surface becomes perfectly <vocabulary>smooth</vocabulary>. 滑らか can describe a smooth surface, motion, or fluent speech.

contextSentences.ja: この布は滑らかな手触りだ。
contextSentences.en: This fabric feels smooth.

contextSentences.ja: 練習して、会話が滑らかになった。
contextSentences.en: Practice made my conversation more fluent.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Build it in an <kanji>instant</kanji> beside your <kanji>seat</kanji> and it is <vocabulary>instant</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>improvised</vocabulary>.

即席 can describe quickly prepared food or something created on the spot with available materials, as in 即席のスープ or 即席の棚.
words.readingMnemonic: Immediate 即 carries そく onto a theater seat 席 carrying せき: <reading>そく—せき</reading>. The seat becomes a cooking stove and produces an <vocabulary>instant</vocabulary>, improvised meal before the audience sits down. 即席 means made on the spot or ready very quickly.

contextSentences.ja: 昼に即席のスープを飲んだ。
contextSentences.en: I had instant soup at lunch.

contextSentences.ja: 箱で即席の棚を作った。
contextSentences.en: I made an improvised shelf from boxes.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Pour <kanji>water</kanji> into a portable <kanji>cylinder</kanji> and you have a <vocabulary>water bottle</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>flask</vocabulary>.

水筒 is a reusable bottle or flask carried with a drink, not an ordinary disposable bottle of water.
words.readingMnemonic: Sue's E-shaped bottle tumbles onto her toe: <reading>SUE—E—TOE</reading>. Water gushes from the <vocabulary>water bottle</vocabulary> and fills her shoe. 水筒 is a portable flask or bottle, commonly carried for drinks.

contextSentences.ja: 水筒に冷たいお茶を入れた。
contextSentences.en: I put cold tea in my water bottle.

contextSentences.ja: 遠足には水筒を持ってきてください。
contextSentences.en: Please bring a water bottle on the field trip.

words.meaningMnemonic:
A bright <kanji>point</kanji> is repeatedly <kanji>destroy</kanji>ed and reborn; the result is <vocabulary>blinking</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>flashing</vocabulary>.

点滅 describes a light switching on and off repeatedly, such as a signal, warning lamp, or low-battery indicator.
words.readingMnemonic: Ten warning lights meet Sue at the door: <reading>TEN—MET—SUE</reading>. They begin <vocabulary>blinking</vocabulary> in sequence until she turns around. 点滅 is repeated switching on and off, as with a light or signal.

contextSentences.ja: 信号が黄色く点滅している。
contextSentences.en: The traffic light is flashing yellow.

contextSentences.ja: 電池が少ないとランプが点滅する。
contextSentences.en: The lamp blinks when the battery is low.

words.meaningMnemonic:
<kanji>White</kanji> <kanji>hair</kanji> is <vocabulary>white hair</vocabulary>, commonly called <vocabulary>gray hair</vocabulary> in English.

白髪 can refer collectively to graying hair or to an individual white strand; 白髪が増える means to get more gray hair.
words.readingMnemonic: A barber begins to shear a ghost. At the first snip, the ghost screams <reading>SHEAR-A—GAH!</reading>, and every cut hair turns into <vocabulary>gray hair</vocabulary>. 白髪 is the ordinary word for gray or white hair, especially hair that has lost its pigment.

contextSentences.ja: 父は最近、白髪が増えた。
contextSentences.en: My father has gotten more gray hair recently.

contextSentences.ja: 鏡を見て一本の白髪を見つけた。
contextSentences.en: I looked in the mirror and found one white hair.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Step away from the <kanji>sun</kanji> and into the cool <kanji>shade</kanji>: the <vocabulary>shade</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>shadow</vocabulary> of 日陰.

日陰 is an area out of direct sunlight, while 影 more generally refers to a cast shadow or silhouette.
words.readingMnemonic: Sun 日 carries ひ into the street, while shadow 陰 carries かげ beneath an umbrella: <reading>ひ—かげ</reading>. Wherever the umbrella moves, it creates cool <vocabulary>shade</vocabulary>. 日陰 is a shaded place or the shade itself.

contextSentences.ja: 暑いので日陰で休みましょう。
contextSentences.en: It is hot, so let's rest in the shade.

contextSentences.ja: 日陰にはまだ雪が残っている。
contextSentences.en: Snow still remains in the shaded areas.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Measure how <kanji>damp</kanji> the air is by <kanji>degree</kanji> and you get its <vocabulary>humidity</vocabulary>.

湿度 is the measured moisture level in the air and commonly appears with 高い, 低い, or a percentage.
words.readingMnemonic: In a tropical bakery, <reading>SHEETS—DOUGH</reading> stick together in the air. The baker peels the damp sheets off the dough and blames the crushing <vocabulary>humidity</vocabulary>. 湿度 is the measured degree of humidity.

contextSentences.ja: 今日は湿度が高くて蒸し暑い。
contextSentences.en: It is humid and muggy today.

contextSentences.ja: 部屋の湿度を五十パーセントに保つ。
contextSentences.en: I keep the room's humidity at fifty percent.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Take each <kanji>tooth</kanji> and <kanji>polish</kanji> it: that is <vocabulary>toothbrushing</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>brushing teeth</vocabulary>.

歯磨き names the routine or act of brushing; 歯磨きをする is to brush one's teeth, while 歯磨き粉 is toothpaste.
words.readingMnemonic: Tooth 歯 carries は into a bathroom, while polish 磨き carries みがき onto a giant brush: <reading>は—みがき</reading>. The brush unlocks after every meal for heroic <vocabulary>toothbrushing</vocabulary>. 歯磨き can mean the act of brushing teeth or toothpaste in some contexts.

contextSentences.ja: 朝晩の歯磨きを忘れないで。
contextSentences.en: Do not forget to brush your teeth morning and night.

contextSentences.ja: 食後に三分間、歯磨きをする。
contextSentences.en: I brush my teeth for three minutes after meals.

packs.title: Everyday Kanji: Levels 46–50
packs.description: High-utility everyday vocabulary whose newest WaniKani kanji falls between levels 46 and 50.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Add り to <kanji>pride</kanji> and turn the feeling into something you carry: <vocabulary>pride</vocabulary>.

誇り is positive dignity or satisfaction in a person, place, achievement, or work; 誇りを持つ means to take pride in it.
words.readingMnemonic: A proud champion displays a trophy, but it is buried under ほこり, dust. Brush off that exact-homophone <reading>ほこり</reading> and reveal the champion's shining <vocabulary>pride</vocabulary>. 誇り is pride in a person, place, ability, or achievement.

contextSentences.ja: 自分の仕事に誇りを持っている。
contextSentences.en: I take pride in my work.

contextSentences.ja: この町の歴史は住民の誇りです。
contextSentences.en: This town's history is a source of pride for its residents.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Every transaction that can <kanji>pass through</kanji> your account is recorded in a <kanji>notebook</kanji>: a <vocabulary>bankbook</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>passbook</vocabulary>.

通帳 is the bank-issued record book used to print deposits, withdrawals, and balances; 通帳に記帳する means to update it.
words.readingMnemonic: PASS THROUGH 通 drills a tunnel through NOTEBOOK 帳; their familiar sounds join as <reading>つう—ちょう</reading>. Every deposit and withdrawal races through the pages of the glowing <vocabulary>bankbook</vocabulary>. 通帳 is a passbook recording bank account transactions.

contextSentences.ja: 銀行で新しい通帳を受け取った。
contextSentences.en: I received a new bankbook at the bank.

contextSentences.ja: 通帳に記帳して残高を確認した。
contextSentences.en: I updated my passbook and checked the balance.

words.meaningMnemonic:
<kanji>Exchange</kanji> stale <kanji>energy</kanji> for fresh air with a spinning <kanji>folding fan</kanji>: a <vocabulary>ventilation fan</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>extractor fan</vocabulary>.

換気扇 is the powered fan that vents air from a kitchen, bathroom, or room; 換気扇を回す means to turn it on.
words.readingMnemonic: Exchange 換 carries かん into a smoky room, air 気 carries き to the window, and fan 扇 carries せん through the wall: <reading>かん—き—せん</reading>. The roaring <vocabulary>ventilation fan</vocabulary> throws smoke and smells outside. 換気扇 is an extractor or exhaust fan used to ventilate a room.

contextSentences.ja: 料理をする前に換気扇を回した。
contextSentences.en: I turned on the extractor fan before cooking.

contextSentences.ja: 換気扇の音が少し大きい。
contextSentences.en: The ventilation fan is a little noisy.

words.meaningMnemonic:
<kanji>Boil</kanji> flavor deep <kanji>into</kanji> the ingredients over time and you <vocabulary>simmer</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>stew</vocabulary> them.

煮込む is a transitive verb for cooking ingredients thoroughly in liquid, usually for longer than a quick boil.
words.readingMnemonic: Boil 煮 carries に into a pot, while pack in 込む carries こむ beneath the lid: <reading>に—こむ</reading>. The ingredients refuse to come out until they <vocabulary>simmer</vocabulary> in the sauce. 煮込む means to cook ingredients thoroughly in liquid, often for some time.

contextSentences.ja: 肉を弱火で二時間煮込む。
contextSentences.en: I simmer the meat over low heat for two hours.

contextSentences.ja: 野菜を煮込むとスープが甘くなる。
contextSentences.en: Stewing the vegetables makes the soup sweeter.

words.meaningMnemonic:
A shopper buys <kanji>nothing</kanji> useful, drags a <kanji>burdensome</kanji> cart of junk to the door, then tells the clerk to <kanji>dispatch</kanji> every coin from their wallet: <vocabulary>wasteful spending</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>squandering</vocabulary>.

無駄遣い can waste money, time, materials, or ability; Xを無駄遣いする means to squander X.
words.readingMnemonic: Waste 無駄 carries むだ onto a credit card, while use 遣い carries つかい toward a luxury shop. The card's impact voices つ to づ in <reading>むだ—づかい</reading>, and diamond-studded hay empties the budget in one burst of <vocabulary>wasteful spending</vocabulary>. 無駄遣い can waste money, time, or resources.

contextSentences.ja: セールで必要のない物を買うのは無駄遣いだ。
contextSentences.en: Buying things you do not need in a sale is wasteful spending.

contextSentences.ja: 時間を無駄遣いしないように計画を立てた。
contextSentences.en: I made a plan so that I would not squander my time.

packs.description: High-utility everyday vocabulary whose newest WaniKani kanji falls between levels 51 and 55.

words.meaningMnemonic:
When something begins to <kanji>wither</kanji>, each <kanji>leaf</kanji> becomes a <vocabulary>dead leaf</vocabulary>; together they are <vocabulary>dry leaves</vocabulary>.

枯れ葉 refers to leaves that have dried and died, especially fallen autumn leaves, and is also commonly written 枯葉.
words.readingMnemonic: Wither 枯れ carries かれ into a tree, and leaf 葉 carries は onto one brittle branch: <reading>かれ—は</reading>. The branch snaps and coughs up a <vocabulary>dead leaf</vocabulary>. 枯れ葉 means a withered or dead leaf; 落ち葉 instead focuses on a leaf that has fallen.

contextSentences.ja: 秋になると庭に枯れ葉が積もる。
contextSentences.en: Dead leaves pile up in the garden in autumn.

contextSentences.ja: 道の枯れ葉をほうきで掃いた。
contextSentences.en: I swept the dry leaves from the road with a broom.

words.meaningMnemonic:
The <kanji>summit</kanji> sitting <kanji>above</kanji> everything else is the <vocabulary>summit</vocabulary>, <vocabulary>peak</vocabulary>, or <vocabulary>top</vocabulary>.

頂上 most often means the top of a mountain, but it can also describe the highest point of another structure or ranking.
words.readingMnemonic: SUMMIT 頂 climbs on top of ABOVE 上, and their familiar on'yomi lock together as <reading>ちょう—じょう</reading>. The stacked kanji balance on the mountain's final rock, marking the <vocabulary>summit</vocabulary>. 頂上 is the highest point or top, especially of a mountain.

contextSentences.ja: 山の頂上から湖が見えた。
contextSentences.en: We could see the lake from the summit of the mountain.

contextSentences.ja: 昼前に頂上へ着いた。
contextSentences.en: We reached the peak before noon.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Line up a <kanji>crown</kanji> ceremony, <kanji>marriage</kanji>, <kanji>burial</kanji>, and <kanji>festival</kanji>; together they represent major <vocabulary>family ceremonies</vocabulary> and <vocabulary>ceremonial occasions</vocabulary>.

冠婚葬祭 is an umbrella term for life's formal rites and the etiquette, clothing, gifts, and obligations surrounding them.
words.readingMnemonic: One family day goes completely wrong: a giant CAN wears the ceremonial crown, a CON artist crashes the wedding, the mourners SEW a funeral veil, and everyone lets out a SIGH when festival fireworks start before the burial ends. <reading>CAN—CON—SEW—SIGH</reading> carries the impossible parade through all the family's major <vocabulary>ceremonial occasions</vocabulary>. 冠婚葬祭 is an umbrella term for major family and life ceremonies and their etiquette, not one particular event.

contextSentences.ja: 冠婚葬祭で着られる黒い服を買った。
contextSentences.en: I bought black clothes suitable for family ceremonies.

contextSentences.ja: 冠婚葬祭のマナーを本で学んだ。
contextSentences.en: I learned the etiquette for ceremonial occasions from a book.

words.meaningMnemonic:
A <kanji>bias</kanji> tilts a test score away from the average; a printer measures the <kanji>difference</kanji> and stamps it as a <kanji>value</kanji>: a <vocabulary>deviation score</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>standardized score</vocabulary>.

偏差値 is a Japanese standardized score used especially for exams and school selectivity, with 50 representing the reference average.
words.readingMnemonic: Deviation 偏差 carries へんさ onto an exam sheet, while value 値 carries ち onto the score: <reading>へんさ—ち</reading>. A hen's result shifts against every other student's to produce a <vocabulary>standardized score</vocabulary>. 偏差値 is commonly used for academic test performance and school selectivity.

contextSentences.ja: 志望校の偏差値を調べた。
contextSentences.en: I looked up the standardized score for my preferred school.

contextSentences.ja: 模試の偏差値が前回より上がった。
contextSentences.en: My practice-test deviation score went up from last time.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Picture the <kanji>wind</kanji> entering a <kanji>bath</kanji> and lifting a cloth you had <kanji>spread</kanji> out: grab that <vocabulary>furoshiki</vocabulary>, the Japanese <vocabulary>wrapping cloth</vocabulary>.

風呂敷 is a reusable square cloth folded and tied around gifts or belongings; the component scene is a memory aid, not a claim about the word's origin.
words.readingMnemonic: A square wrapping cloth sprouts a giant 'fro, points to a woman, and swallows her key: <reading>FRO—SHE—KEY</reading>. She unfolds the <vocabulary>furoshiki</vocabulary> and turns it into a bag for carrying the key home. 風呂敷 is a reusable wrapping cloth, not a bath towel.

contextSentences.ja: 贈り物を風呂敷で包んだ。
contextSentences.en: I wrapped the gift in a furoshiki.

contextSentences.ja: この風呂敷は小さく畳める。
contextSentences.en: This wrapping cloth folds up small.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Repeat <kanji>gently</kanji> with 々 and add に: change now unfolds <vocabulary>gradually</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>steadily</vocabulary>.

徐々に is an adverb for progressive change by small degrees, often with verbs such as 増える, 減る, or 慣れる.
words.readingMnemonic: Two men named Joe lower themselves onto one knee in tiny synchronized steps: <reading>JOE—JOE—KNEE</reading>. Their exaggerated slow motion moves them <vocabulary>gradually</vocabulary> toward the floor. 徐々に describes change happening little by little over time.

contextSentences.ja: 空が徐々に明るくなった。
contextSentences.en: The sky gradually grew brighter.

contextSentences.ja: 痛みは徐々に弱くなっている。
contextSentences.en: The pain is steadily becoming weaker.

words.meaningMnemonic:
For an <kanji>original</kanji> <kanji>draft</kanji>, <kanji>use</kanji> each square of <kanji>paper</kanji> for one character: <vocabulary>Japanese manuscript paper</vocabulary>, or <vocabulary>manuscript paper</vocabulary>.

原稿用紙 is paper printed with squares for Japanese composition, traditionally with one character or punctuation mark per square.
words.readingMnemonic: Manuscript 原稿 carries げんこう onto a gridded sheet, while writing paper 用紙 carries ようし into a paper dragon: <reading>げんこう—ようし</reading>. The dragon stamps every square, transforming the sheet into <vocabulary>Japanese manuscript paper</vocabulary>. 原稿用紙 is the ruled square paper used for handwritten Japanese manuscripts or school compositions.

contextSentences.ja: 作文を原稿用紙に書いた。
contextSentences.en: I wrote the composition on Japanese manuscript paper.

contextSentences.ja: 原稿用紙を三枚使いました。
contextSentences.en: I used three sheets of manuscript paper.

words.meaningMnemonic:
<kanji>Install</kanji> something, <kanji>put</kanji> it there, and refuse to move it: it is <vocabulary>left unchanged</vocabulary>, or the decision is a <vocabulary>deferment</vocabulary>.

据え置き often means keeping a price, rate, policy, or status at its current level rather than raising, lowering, or acting on it.
words.readingMnemonic: Clerk Sue hesitates, “Eh?”, then sets an old key beside the price tag: <reading>SUE—EH—OH—KEY</reading>. She leaves the number exactly where it was, so the price is <vocabulary>left unchanged</vocabulary>. 据え置き can mean keeping a price or rate unchanged, leaving equipment installed, or deferring action.

contextSentences.ja: 来年も料金は据え置きです。
contextSentences.en: The fee will be left unchanged next year.

contextSentences.ja: 金利の据え置きが発表された。
contextSentences.en: A decision to leave interest rates unchanged was announced.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Make a tiny object <kanji>appear</kanji>, reveal its <kanji>delicate</kanji> details, and reflect them through a <kanji>mirror</kanji>: you are using a <vocabulary>microscope</vocabulary>.

顕微鏡 is the scientific instrument used to observe cells, microbes, and other objects too small to see unaided.
words.readingMnemonic: Visible 顕 carries けん onto a bee, minute 微 carries び into its wing hairs, and mirror 鏡 carries きょう into a huge lens: <reading>けん—び—きょう</reading>. The invisible hairs fill the screen through the <vocabulary>microscope</vocabulary>. 顕微鏡 is an instrument for magnifying tiny objects.

contextSentences.ja: 顕微鏡で細胞を観察した。
contextSentences.en: I observed cells through a microscope.

contextSentences.ja: 学校の顕微鏡を丁寧に運んだ。
contextSentences.en: I carefully carried the school's microscope.

words.meaningMnemonic:
A <kanji>coarse</kanji> job that stops before the proper <kanji>end</kanji> looks <vocabulary>crude</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>shabby</vocabulary>, and its offering may be <vocabulary>meager</vocabulary>.

粗末 describes poor quality, scant provision, or careless treatment; 粗末にする means to treat something as unimportant or waste it.
words.readingMnemonic: Sue sleeps on a splintered mat and groans, <reading>SO—MAT—SUE!</reading> The <vocabulary>shabby</vocabulary>, crude bedding collapses before morning. 粗末 can describe poor-quality things or careless treatment of something.

contextSentences.ja: 昼食はパン一枚だけの粗末なものだった。
contextSentences.en: Lunch was a meager meal of only one slice of bread.

contextSentences.ja: 粗末な小屋で雨をしのいだ。
contextSentences.en: We took shelter from the rain in a shabby hut.

words.meaningMnemonic:
If <kanji>sugar</kanji> appears in <kanji>urine</kanji>, it can warn that someone is <kanji>sick</kanji> with <vocabulary>diabetes</vocabulary>.

糖尿病 is the standard medical term for diabetes; diagnosis depends on clinical testing, not on this composition mnemonic.
words.readingMnemonic: A doctor's model links a sugar cube, a urine sample, and a flashing illness alarm while the labels pulse <reading>TOU—NYOU—BYOU</reading>. Together they identify <vocabulary>diabetes</vocabulary>, and the model sends the patient to proper care. 糖尿病 is the medical term for diabetes; the three established on-reading chunks carry the whole sound.

contextSentences.ja: 医師から糖尿病について説明を受けた。
contextSentences.en: A doctor explained diabetes to me.

contextSentences.ja: 運動は糖尿病の予防に役立つ。
contextSentences.en: Exercise helps prevent diabetes.

words.meaningMnemonic:
<kanji>Try</kanji>, <kanji>go</kanji>, become <kanji>confused</kanji>, find the <kanji>mistake</kanji>, and try again; the cycle is <vocabulary>trial and error</vocabulary>.

試行錯誤 emphasizes repeated experimentation and adjustment while searching for a workable method or solution.
words.readingMnemonic: A mad inventor runs a trial, hits an error, and resets while four signs flash <reading>SHI—KOU—SAKU—GO</reading>. Each failed machine teaches her something, so she reaches the solution through <vocabulary>trial and error</vocabulary>. 試行錯誤 emphasizes repeated attempts and mistakes in finding a solution.

contextSentences.ja: 試行錯誤を重ねて方法を見つけた。
contextSentences.en: After repeated trial and error, I found a method.

contextSentences.ja: 新しい料理を試行錯誤しながら作った。
contextSentences.en: I developed the new dish through trial and error.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Build an <kanji>imitation</kanji> exam room to <kanji>imitate</kanji> real conditions, then <kanji>try</kanji> every question before the real <kanji>test</kanji>: a <vocabulary>mock exam</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>practice test</vocabulary>.

模擬試験 reproduces exam conditions for practice and assessment before the actual examination; 模試 is its common abbreviation.
words.readingMnemonic: Imitation 模擬 carries もぎ into a fake exam hall, while test 試験 carries しけん onto every desk: <reading>もぎ—しけん</reading>. The room looks official, but everyone is taking only a <vocabulary>mock exam</vocabulary>. 模擬試験 is a practice test designed to imitate the real examination.

contextSentences.ja: 日曜日に模擬試験を受ける。
contextSentences.en: I'm taking a mock exam on Sunday.

contextSentences.ja: 模擬試験の結果を先生と確認した。
contextSentences.en: I reviewed the practice-test results with my teacher.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Add わしい to <kanji>annoy</kanji> and stretch the irritation into an adjective: <vocabulary>troublesome</vocabulary>, <vocabulary>annoying</vocabulary>, or <vocabulary>complicated</vocabulary>.

煩わしい describes a procedure, task, relationship, or situation that causes persistent bother through effort or complexity.
words.readingMnemonic: A witness begins, ‘It WAS—,’ but a cheerleader interrupts ‘RAH!’, a washer screams ‘WASH!’, and a giant letter E crashes through the roof.
